title: Translational execution lanes: Q3 OKRs -> Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: convert Q3 strategic OKRs into a concrete, time-boxed set of execution lanes that align Hosted API launch commitments with the Model Catalog curation, canary cadence, and capacity hedges. This ticket is the PM playbook artifact that will: (1) define three execution lanes (Core Launch, Capacity Hedge, Quality Guardrails); (2) map owners, milestones, and SLOs; (3) enumerate evals and gating criteria for each lane; and (4) surface cross-team risks and mitigation plans.

Scope: hosted endpoints (public API), model catalog onboarding/pruning, canary windows and rollback policies, and customer-facing release messaging. Non-goals: dedicated/private deployment changes (handled in separate initiative).

Success metrics (proposed):
- End-of-quarter: 90% of hosted endpoints in the catalog have a defined canary policy and evaluation harness.
- Canary failure early-detection: mean time from regression detection to rollback < 30m for P1 regressions.
- Cost hedging: identified and validated two alternate model variants that reduce per-token cost by >= 15% for the 20% highest-traffic routes.

Key deliverables:
- Lane definitions & owner RACI (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/q3-translational-lanes)
- Canary gating matrix + eval spec (drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/fake-eval-specs-q3)
- Runbook snippets for rollouts + emergency rollback (GH gist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/rollout-lanes)
- Dashboard mocks for per-lane SLOs and cost impact (Metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hostedapi-lanes)

Trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressive pruning of older catalog models reduces maintenance overhead but increases short-term customer risk; proposed compromise is a 3-stage prune window with a shadow routing period.
- Tight canary windows reduce exposure time but increase manual ops; we recommend automated regression detection for token-level anomalies to reduce manual intervention.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Maya Chen (lead), Product Strategy: Jonas Rivera, Eng Leads: Priya Patel (runtime), Aaron Kim (platform), Design: Sofia Morales, Reliability: Tom Becker, Evals: Nina Rao.

Risks & blockers:
- Dependency ENG-1842 (improved KV cache snapshotting) must land by 2026-04-20 to enable low-latency canaries for long-context models.
- Capacity simulation data is incomplete; data request ticket ENG-9031 must resolve before capacity hedges can be finalized.

Next steps (by 2026-03-17):
1) Consolidate lane owners and finalize RACI (owner: Maya Chen).
2) PM/Eng working session to finalize eval gating metrics (owner: Liam O'Neill).
3) Design to produce two lightweight dashboard mocks for SLO signoffs (owner: Sofia Morales).
4) Schedule cross-functional kickoff + exec readout for week of 2026-03-22.

Notes: this ticket serves as the canonical mapping between Q3 OKRs (OKR-HOSTED-01: "predictable 99th percentile latency for top 50 routes" and OKR-CATALOG-02: "reduce model maintenance cost by 20%") and the concrete engineering deliverables. Keep PRD links and runbook changes attached to this ticket for traceability.
